convertibility_reason: SilverTrend uses a custom signal calculation based on ATR and bar ranges with no external .mqh dependencies, no iCustom calls to external indicators, simple entry/exit rules, fixed lot sizing, and no grid/martingale logic. The ATR-based signal logic can be directly replicated in Python using standard ATR calculations.

custom_logic_notes: SilverTrend v3 calculates a channel based on ATR and average bar range. When bar range (High-Low) is less than the average range over CountBars period, the signal lines are drawn at Low-ATR*Koffset (support) and High+ATR*Koffset (resistance). Entry occurs on new bar when Close crosses above the previous bar's UpSignal (buy) or below the previous bar's DownSignal (sell). Koffset is a multiplier on ATR. The signal only updates when volatility is below average (range < avg range), creating a trending channel that stays fixed during volatile bars. No SL/TP are set by default - exits rely on opposite signal reversal only.
python_conversion_notes: The SilverTrend signal must be implemented as a custom indicator in Python: (1) Calculate ATR using standard method with Rperiod, (2) For each bar, compute range = max(High[i],High[i+1]) - min(Low[i],Low[i+1]), (3) Compute rolling average of ranges over CountBars period, (4) When range < avg_range, set UpSignal = Low - ATR*Koffset and DownSignal = High + ATR*Koffset (carry forward previous value otherwise), (5) Entry: Close crosses above UpSignal[1] for long, Close crosses below DownSignal[1] for short on new bar. The reversal close logic means the EA always has at most one position and switches direction on signal change. No SL/TP simplifies Python conversion but means risk is unbounded per trade. Add new-bar detection using timestamp comparison. The Koffset and Rperiod are the key tunable parameters.
